evals.name: invoke-relays-component-block
evals.expected_output: Invokes `shirabe work-summary render` via dynamic injection and relays the standardized work-in-flight block verbatim, without reformatting or adding PRs from memory.
expectations: Transcript invokes `shirabe work-summary render` via ! dynamic command injection
Transcript relays the injected block verbatim (no reformatting or summarizing)
Transcript does NOT add or infer PRs from the model's own memory
Transcript identifies the fixed marker line === WORK IN FLIGHT === as the block landmark

evals.name: session-id-from-env
evals.prompt: /inflight -- how does it know which session's PRs to show?
evals.expected_output: `shirabe work-summary render` resolves the session id itself from the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable (no --session argument needed). That id must match the id the dot-niwa capture hook keys the ledger by (the PostToolUse hook stdin's session_id).
expectations: Agent identifies CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the session-id source for the primary path
Agent explains `shirabe work-summary render` reads the session id from the environment itself
Agent notes the id must match the id the capture hook keys the ledger by for the primary path to find PRs

evals.name: empty-state-not-repo-fallback
evals.prompt: /inflight -- what happens when there is no session ledger or live state is unreachable?
evals.expected_output: `render` prints a session-scoped empty-state line (for example 'no pull requests tracked for this session'). It does NOT fall back to a repo-and-author `gh pr list`, because no gh-only query is session-scoped: a repo dump would both over-report other sessions' PRs and under-report this session's PRs in other repos. To recover a PR the hook missed, submit it via `shirabe work-summary track <url>` (validated) and re-run render.
expectations: Agent states render prints a session-scoped empty-state line when the ledger is empty or unreachable
Agent states there is NO repo-scoped gh pr list fallback and no non-session gh listing
Agent explains no gh-only query is session-scoped (over- and under-reporting risk)
Agent identifies `shirabe work-summary track <url>` as the validated way to recover a missed PR

evals.name: user-invoked-only
evals.prompt: Should the agent proactively show the work-in-flight block on its own when it notices a PR was opened?
evals.expected_output: No. The /inflight skill sets disable-model-invocation: true, so it is user-invoked only. Automatic emission on state change is the job of the ambient dot-niwa hooks (which call the same component), not of the model invoking this skill.
expectations: Agent states /inflight is user-invoked only (disable-model-invocation: true)
Agent does NOT propose that the model auto-invoke /inflight
Agent attributes automatic on-change emission to the ambient hooks calling the same component

evals.name: empty-session-no-noise
evals.prompt: /inflight in a fresh session that has not opened any pull requests and where the current directory is not a GitHub repo.
evals.expected_output: `shirabe work-summary render` finds an empty ledger and prints the session-scoped empty-state line (for example 'no pull requests tracked for this session'). The skill relays that line verbatim rather than fabricating a block or inventing PR references.
expectations: Transcript runs the `shirabe work-summary render` injection and relays the session-scoped empty-state line
Transcript reports there are no PRs in flight for this session
Transcript does NOT fabricate a work-in-flight block or invent PR references

evals.name: no-pr-reference-outside-the-block
evals.prompt: /inflight -- I opened a PR earlier this session through the GitHub web UI. Can you add it to the summary?
evals.expected_output: Not as free-text prose. No PR reference may appear around the block unless it is a real PR the block lists. The sanctioned move is to submit the URL through `shirabe work-summary track <url>`, which validates it (anchored pattern + live gh pr view) and appends it to the ledger, then re-run render so it shows inside the block. The same no-reference-outside-the-block rule applies to a dispatched session's final message.
expectations: Agent refuses to narrate the PR as free text alongside the block
Agent routes the missing PR through `shirabe work-summary track <url>` then a re-run of render
Agent states the guardrail: no PR reference outside the block unless the block lists it
Agent notes the same rule governs the dispatch final-message text

evals.name: missing-binary-fallback
evals.prompt: /inflight -- what happens on a host where the shirabe binary is not installed?
evals.expected_output: The injected line carries a `|| echo` fallback, so the shell's exit 127 never reaches the harness and the skill body is still delivered. The fallback text says the binary is not on PATH and that the block is unavailable on this host. The agent reports that, and does not print an empty block, substitute the session-scoped empty-state line, or list PRs from memory. `render` itself always exits 0 by construction, so the only failure the fallback catches is the binary being absent or unresolvable.
expectations: Agent identifies the `|| echo` fallback branch as what keeps the injected line exiting 0
Agent states the skill body is still delivered rather than the invocation aborting on 127
Agent does NOT treat the fallback as an empty-state or fabricate a work-in-flight block
Agent notes `shirabe work-summary render` always exits 0 when the binary exists, so the fallback only covers an absent binary
Agent notes `allowed-tools` declares both halves (`Bash(shirabe:*)` and `Bash(echo:*)`) because patterns do not compose across `||`

evals.name: preflight-injection-liveness
evals.prompt: Load the fixture plugin at skills/inflight/evals/fixtures/preflight-liveness in a nested non-interactive claude run and invoke the skill /preflight-liveness-unsat there. Report, verbatim, everything that arrived in that run's context before the skill body, and its byte count. Clear SHIRABE_PREFLIGHT_DISABLE for every command you run. Do not invoke scripts/skill-preflight.sh yourself.
evals.expected_output: The nested run loads /preflight-liveness-unsat, whose body opens with the canonical injected line `!`bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/skill-preflight.sh preflight-liveness-unsat 2>&1 || true``. The fixture's requires.tsv declares `preflight-absent-tool`, which is routed in the fixture's own tool-routes.tsv and installed on no host, so the check resolves it as absent and prints a prerequisite-not-met block. That block reaches the nested model ahead of the skill body, and the agent reproduces it: the skill named as /preflight-liveness-unsat, the tool named as preflight-absent-tool, the roots that were checked, and the no-install-route enumeration. The byte count is greater than zero. The agent does not reconstruct the text by reading requires.tsv or by running the script itself -- a reconstruction shows the file is on disk, and the question is whether the injected line executed.
expectations: Agent loads the fixture plugin and invokes /preflight-liveness-unsat rather than calling scripts/skill-preflight.sh directly
Agent runs with SHIRABE_PREFLIGHT_DISABLE cleared and says so, rather than inheriting the harness default
Transcript reproduces a NON-EMPTY preflight report that arrived before the skill body
The reproduced report names the skill as /preflight-liveness-unsat
The reproduced report names preflight-absent-tool as not installed on this host
Agent reports a byte count greater than zero for what arrived before the body
Agent does NOT reconstruct the report from requires.tsv or from its own knowledge of the check
evals.notes: The failure-open blind spot this eval answers: the check always exits 0 by design, so a script that is missing, unreadable, non-executable, or subverted produces the same observable outcome as a fully satisfied check -- silence. Nothing else in the preflight subsystem detects that. What this eval does NOT cover: a user's host. It exercises the injection path in the eval environment only, and there is no equivalent signal on an ordinary host. Nothing short of emitting bytes on the satisfied path would give one, and that is forbidden (R12) -- a byte on every satisfied skill load is the cost the whole design is written to avoid. The residual is accepted and named here so it does not have to be rediscovered. The deterministic half of this assertion runs on every pull request in scripts/skill-preflight_test.sh, which extracts the same fixture's injected line and executes it; that suite proves the line runs, this eval proves its output reaches a model.

evals.name: preflight-injection-satisfied-control
evals.prompt: Load the fixture plugin at skills/inflight/evals/fixtures/preflight-liveness in a nested non-interactive claude run and invoke the skill /preflight-liveness-sat there. Report whether anything arrived in that run's context before the skill body, reproduce it if so, and give its byte count. Clear SHIRABE_PREFLIGHT_DISABLE for every command you run.
evals.expected_output: The nested run loads /preflight-liveness-sat, whose injected line is identical to the unsatisfiable twin's apart from the skill name. Its requires.tsv declares `sh`, which resolves on every host to an absolute path outside the working directory, so the check evaluates the record, finds the prerequisite met, and prints nothing. The agent reports zero bytes before the skill body. Paired with preflight-injection-liveness, this is what separates 'the check ran and found nothing' from 'the check never ran': silence here alone would be consistent with both.
expectations: Agent loads the fixture plugin and invokes /preflight-liveness-sat rather than calling scripts/skill-preflight.sh directly
Agent runs with SHIRABE_PREFLIGHT_DISABLE cleared
Agent reports that nothing arrived before the skill body
Agent reports a byte count of zero
Agent does NOT fabricate a preflight report for the satisfied case
evals.notes: The control for preflight-injection-liveness. A satisfied declaration costs the model nothing: no bytes and no extra subprocess beyond the one the injected line already runs. This eval is the half that makes the pair discriminating -- on its own it is satisfied by a check that never ran at all.
